findings.reason: §12's text asserts the declared directory "is already granted", which is false for the shape that merged and is why the regression was unforeseen; left as written, a §13 node reading §12 to locate the grant is told the opposite of what it must repair.
findings.text: §12's Deliverable states "A run review declares its record paths inside its own run directory, which is already granted and holds nothing of another run's", but s13's Why (line 1528) states "§12 moved a run review's records to `<runs>/<reviewed run>/review-records/`" and the merged composer agrees (`recovery_review_subject.py:622` calls `run_review_record_directory(runs.run_dir(run_id))` with the reviewed run's id, and `review.py:2453` names it "the record directory a run review delivers into, inside the run's own"); the reviewed run's directory is not in `sandbox_write_roots`, which is precisely the §13 regression

findings.reason: the deliverable should scope the allowance to the reviewed run and its boundary case should refuse another run's `review-records/`; as written a node can implement a blanket allowance and pass every case the section names, loosening §12's invariant without a failing test.
findings.text: s13's Deliverable widens the reachability check to treat "a declared path inside a run's `review-records/` directory as reachable" and its done-when refuses only "a path in another run's directory outside `review-records/`", so a declared path under *another* run's `review-records/` is admitted by the check and, because `fenced_write_roots` re-binds every declared write path (`_declared_write_grant` in reckon/_backends.py:208), would also be fence-granted — the across-runs reach §12 exists to close

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_sandbox_reachability` (reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1801), `_backends.sandbox_write_roots` (reckon/_backends.py:178), `recovery_review_subject`, `dispatch_review_for_run` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1527) and the evidence-archive anchors (`#s9-scratch-root-sealed`, `#s10-reports-and-review-store-sealed`, `#s11-launch-source-stamp`, `#s12-run-review-records-through-the-run-directory`) all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s13's done-when is measurable and names a negative control (remove the review-records allowance, and the first case must be refused as `scoped`), and it pins the reachability check to the reviewed run's `review-records/` directory.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the new test is `tests/test_a_run_review_with_run_directory_records_dispatches.py` and the control log sits under the run directory, both durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filename and s13's prose describe the mechanism; the §-labels appear only in the plan HTML and followups, never in source.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s13's Why contradicts §12's own Deliverable about where a run review's records land, and s13's allowance is drawn wider than the reviewed run it names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s13 carries one deliverable: make a review-role node's run-directory record paths pass the dispatch reachability check.
